clue.text: Let us follow the view of Gray, advertising a college

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the brochure that advertises a college

indicators.note: follow means the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College, so his 'view' is a prospect
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to follow Gray's poetic view of Eton, as if in a college advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's poem looks at Eton College from afar; that 'prospect' is followed by US. The definition is a description, the booklet doing the advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university publishes a brochure describing itself to attract applicants.

clue.text: Fruit that grows feathers with age

indicators.note: the fruit grows into the feathers once the word age is joined on, so taking that word away leaves the fruit
the fruit grows into the feathers once the word age is joined on, so taking that word away leaves the fruit

parts.note: a bird's feathers are its plumage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fruit that sprouts feathers as it gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the fruit plus AGE makes a word for feathers; removing AGE from that feathery word gives the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone fruit with purple or yellow skin, grown on orchard trees.

clue.text: They give a better interest

parts.note: read 'better' as one who bets: bookmakers' prices give a punter a stake in the outcome

explanation.surface: Something that offers a superior rate of interest, like a savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative, but it is a gambler, a bettor; the prices quoted make the race interesting to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' prices set what a winning wager pays, which is what keeps a gambler engaged.

clue.text: One in favour of the classics

definitions.text: One in favour of the classics

parts.words: One in favour of the classics
parts.note: a person who is in favour, described in the language of the classics, Latin

explanation.surface: Someone who supports classical education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In favour of' looks like supporting; it means being favoured, and 'the classics' points to a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin diplomatic phrase for an acceptable or welcome person.

clue.text: They often pop out for drinks

definitions.text: They often pop out for drinks

parts.words: They often pop out for drinks
parts.note: not people going to the pub but bottle stoppers popping when wine is opened

explanation.surface: People who frequently nip out to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of colleagues popping out for a drink; it is the stoppers that pop from bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle stoppers made of bark burst out when champagne is opened.

clue.text: Timely speech which gave Wordsworth's thought relief

definitions.text: Timely speech which gave Wordsworth's thought relief

parts.words: Timely speech which gave Wordsworth's thought relief
parts.note: quotes Wordsworth's Immortality Ode, where 'a timely' word of speech 'gave that thought relief'

explanation.surface: A well-judged remark that eased the poet Wordsworth's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Wordsworth's Ode: Intimations of Immortality: 'A timely ... gave that thought relief'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken remark or expression; the poem uses this word for speech.

clue.text: Put back a portion of gin

definitions.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals

indicators.note: putting something back here means writing the word in reverse order

parts.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: Returning part of a measure of gin to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink; it is the old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching game, a device for catching animals.

clue.text: You could certainly hear this one drop — in the kitchen!

definitions.text: You could certainly hear this one drop — in the kitchen!

parts.words: You could certainly hear this one drop — in the kitchen!
parts.note: plays on 'you could hear a pin drop': this pin is a heavy pastry tool that would clatter

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying about silence being so complete you could hear a pin drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is about a tiny sewing pin; the kitchen kind is a big wooden roller that lands with a thud.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden cylinder used for flattening pastry dough in cooking.

clue.text: Inclination to break nipper's toy

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters so they can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken with its S as letters

explanation.surface: A child's tendency to smash their toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To break' signals rearranging the letters of NIPPER'S TOY; the S of the possessive is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural tendency or leaning towards some behaviour.

clue.text: Subscribe as a matter of policy

definitions.meaning: to subscribe is literally to write one's name below, to sign or guarantee
what an insurer does to an insurance policy, accepting its risk

explanation.surface: Signing up to something as a fixed rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy' looks like a general principle; it is an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign beneath, and in insurance to accept liability for a risk.

clue.text: Thus ran out of place

parts.note: replace 'Thus' with its synonym and the phrase with 'ran' names a horse that finished unplaced

explanation.surface: In this way someone ran out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: Horses that finish outside the places are listed as 'also ran'; the answer is the word that means 'thus' or 'in like manner'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word meaning 'in addition', 'likewise', which with 'ran' describes an unplaced runner.

clue.text: A musical ride here in the Game, nursery

definitions.text: A musical ride here in the Game, nursery

parts.words: A musical ride here in the Game, nursery
parts.note: points to the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock-horse', where the lady with bells on her toes has music wherever she goes

explanation.surface: A tuneful ride as part of a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the ride on a cock-horse ends at this Oxfordshire landmark, with music from rings and bells.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxfordshire market cross named as the destination in the old nursery rhyme.

clue.text: One who might crave votes in a re-shuffle

definitions.text: One who might crave votes in a re-shuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle mixes things up again, so these letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A Tory politician seeking support during a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A re-shuffle' signals rearranging CRAVE VOTES IN, and the whole clue describes a Tory MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory party member is a politician who would canvass for support.

clue.text: One who's existence depends on dripping

definitions.text: One who's existence depends on dripping

parts.words: One who's existence depends on dripping
parts.note: sounds like someone living on beef fat, but describes a limestone formation that hangs from a cave roof, built by drips

explanation.surface: Someone who lives on bread and dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends' is literal: the formation hangs down, made by water dripping in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A limestone spike hanging from a cave ceiling, formed by mineral-laden water drops.

clue.text: Perhaps a rich aunt's paying Cinema his school fees?

definitions.note: the person whose fees are paid, a pupil at Charterhouse school

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A wealthy aunt paying a boy's school fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals rearranging A RICH AUNT'S. A pupil at Charterhouse, a private school in Surrey, is a Carthusian; 'paying Cinema' seems to be a misprint in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Charterhouse, a fee-paying English private school, is known by this name.

clue.text: Cosy sort of place, where caddies provide refreshment

definitions.text: Cosy sort of place, where caddies provide refreshment

parts.words: Cosy sort of place, where caddies provide refreshment
parts.note: cosies and caddies both belong with a drink served in pots: a place for a brew outdoors

explanation.surface: A snug golf club where the caddies serve drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caddies' suggests golf; a tea caddy holds leaves, and a tea cosy keeps the pot warm.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor café or garden where refreshments are served.

clue.text: The crime of Samuel Whiskers?

parts.note: Samuel Whiskers is Beatrix Potter's rat, and rats are said to leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Asking what offence a storybook villain committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Whiskers is a rat in Beatrix Potter; rats proverbially abandon sinking ships, the military crime of going absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning one's post or duty, a military offence.

clue.text: Sham way to go about public transport

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes to, into, the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: going about here means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fake route for getting around by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns GO into OG, which goes into BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something counterfeit or fake.

clue.text: Alter, possibly, but not just yet

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: A decision to change something, but not right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals rearranging ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done afterwards rather than immediately.

clue.text: Plant for the manufacture of old weapons?

definitions.text: Plant for the manufacture of old weapons?

parts.words: Plant for the manufacture of old weapons?
parts.note: a 'plant' as a factory: a mint making lances, though it is the herb

explanation.surface: A factory producing ancient arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory; split the answer as a spear mint and it becomes an arms works, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden herb of the mint family used for flavouring gum.

clue.text: Evolution of protesting shopwalkers?

parts.note: 'evolution' in its military sense, a drill manoeuvre; shop staff at the till going on a protest march

explanation.surface: How a group of protesting store staff develops over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evolution' is a drill movement. Shopwalkers work behind the counter, and protesters march.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill manoeuvre in which troops reverse direction.

clue.text: Our attachment to it is matter of time

definitions.text: Our attachment to it is matter of time

parts.words: Our attachment to it is matter of time
parts.note: the letter attached to 'our' turns it into sixty minutes, a matter of time

explanation.surface: Becoming attached to something takes time.
explanation.walkthrough: Fix the letter H to the front of 'our' and it becomes a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: She may lead the band a dance

definitions.text: She may lead the band a dance

parts.words: She may lead the band a dance
parts.note: a woman's name that goes in front of 'band' to make a stately dance

explanation.surface: A woman giving the musicians the runaround.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the name before BAND and you get the saraband, a slow Spanish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, which also begins the name of a slow dance.

clue.text: Peer of the stage

parts.note: not an aristocrat of the theatre but Ibsen's play hero, whose first name is Peer

explanation.surface: An actor who has been made a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a noble; it is the first name of the title character in Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Ibsen's Norwegian rogue hero, title character of a famous play.

clue.text: She shows the flag in the garden

definitions.text: She shows the flag in the garden

parts.words: She shows the flag in the garden
parts.note: a woman's name that is also a flower, the flag being a kind of lily-like plant

explanation.surface: A patriotic woman flying a flag in her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is another name for the plant; the name also belongs to the Greek rainbow goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name and a garden flower also called the flag.

clue.text: At a loss for words? Try this!

definitions.text: At a loss for words? Try this!

parts.words: At a loss for words? Try this!
parts.note: being lost for words normally means speechless, but here it means stuck for a word to use

explanation.surface: Advice for someone left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a loss for words' means speechless, but taken literally it means needing to look a word up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book listing words with their meanings.

clue.text: Bird from Northern Europe

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A bird native to northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals letters taken from inside NORTHERN EUROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Oddly, the USA isn't for the zealot

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A strange claim that America is not the place for fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'odd letters', but it signals rearranging THE USA ISN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionately devoted to a cause or hobby.
